transcript:
[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. quick intro, i'm Samir from Redwood, this is Laura our SE.
[00:12] Marcus: Hey Samir, hey Laura, Marcus here. we're a small quant team, heavy inference workloads for risk signals.
[00:18] Laura: quick question on the stack, are you running models in prod now?
[00:22] Marcus: yeah we have a mix, mostly huggingface fine-tuned models on SageMaker, some local GPUs for high-priority jobs. latency is... kinda variable.
[00:30] Aisha: to add, budget is constrained this quarter, Ben will chime in on the exact figures.
[00:35] Ben: hi all, yes we have a $120k quarterly budget for inference, need to understand unit economics before we commit.
[00:42] Samir: perfect. today we'll focus on cost per token, how batching and KV/prefix caching can move the needle, and tradeoffs between Hosted, Dedicated, and Private.
[00:50] Laura: quick high level — Redwood hosted is simplest, pay-as-you-go per token. Dedicated is reserved capacity — predictable throughput and lower unit cost at steady state. Private is for VPC/on-prem for compliance.
[01:05] Marcus: ok can you give ballpark per-token numbers? we've seen wide variance, and the high context lengths we use blow up costs.
[01:12] Samir: sure, rough ranges — hosted for large open models we've verified is around $0.0009 to $0.0018 per input+output token depending on model and quant. Dedicated, on a reserved commit, can get you 30-50% lower unit costs, maybe $0.0005 to $0.001. these are ballparks, we'll send spreadsheet.
[01:30] Aisha: how much of that is influenced by batching? our workloads are bursty but with microbursts of 20-30 concurrent requests.
[01:40] Laura: batching matters a lot. if you can tolerate a 10-30ms extra queuing we can batch and amortize context compute, cutting per-token by up to 20-40% depending on sequence lengths. continuous batching in the runtime also helps during steady qps.
[01:56] Marcus: we mostly do 2-3k tokens per request, sometimes up to 8k.
[02:02] Samir: right so some levers: 1) batch size / latency SLO tradeoff, 2) prefix/KV caching for common prompts (saves generation cost), 3) quantization and model variant routing to cheaper variants when acceptable.
[02:18] Ben: can you quantify caching? how many tokens saved?
[02:22] Laura: depends on prompt reuse. we've seen prefix caching save 30-70% token generation for chat-like workloads where the prefix is large. KV cache reduces re-computation in long context scenarios, so for reco systems with long state it can be 40%+.
[02:37] Marcus: hmm we do a lot of long-context risk logs, KV cache sounds good. are there tradeoffs for latency?
[02:42] Laura: small overhead on cache lookup but massive downstream savings on generation. the runtime is optimized to keep KV in GPU memory for hot sessions.
[02:50] Marcus: what about private deployment costs — do we lose the batching benefits?
[02:55] Samir: private can still use the same runtime and batching; the difference is infra cost (you manage or we ship appliances). unit economics depend on your infra pricing. Dedicated gives the best middle ground — Redwood manages infra with reserved GPUs and you get the low unit costs without ops overhead.
[03:12] Aisha: ok timeline: we need pilot results within 2 weeks to feed procurement. can you do that?
[03:18] Samir: yes we can run a week-long small pilot; Laura will own the benchmark plan.
[03:22] Laura: i'll need sample queries, typical qps, P95 latency targets, and expected concurrency. Marcus can you share a redacted dataset?
[03:30] Marcus: yes we'll prepare a masked subset, maybe 50K requests, is that enough?
[03:35] Laura: perfect. that's enough for an initial cost econ run.
[03:38] Ben: procurement question: if we go Dedicated, what's commitment term and exit?
[03:43] Samir: typical reserved is quarterly or annual, with flexible burst and canary policies. we can structure a 3-month pilot that doesn't lock you long-term and converts to reserved once you like the numbers.
[03:55] Marcus: i want to understand the per-token delta at P95 latencies. can you show us a worked example?
[04:00] Samir: sure, quick worked example — assume model costs X on hosted, with batching we drop per-token by Y, with dedicated reserved capacity plus aggressive quant we might cut another 20%. we'll send exact calcs.
[04:14] Aisha: clarify quantization impact on quality — we can't afford regressions that affect trading signals.
[04:20] Laura: totally. we recommend sample-based evals — run your evals against quantized variants and our team flags regressions. small regressions sometimes acceptable, we can route critical workflows to full-precision variants.
[04:35] Marcus: routing sounds useful — automatic fallback?
[04:38] Samir: yes policy-based routing by latency, cost, and model quality. for example, cheaper quant variant for bulk scoring, full-precision for top-N rerank.
[04:47] Ben: how do we measure unit economics? do you provide dashboards?
[04:51] Samir: Redwood Console has token-level cost breakdown, per-route/model dashboards, and estimated monthly spend. We'll share a demo link.
[05:00] Aisha: security — we need SOC2, audit logs, KMS, and SSO. can you support?
[05:06] Laura: yes, hosted supports audit logs, customer-managed KMS for Dedicated/Private, SSO via SAML/OKTA, SOC2 cert available.
[05:13] Marcus: any gotchas around data residency? we operate in eu and us.
[05:18] Samir: we have region routing and private deployments for strict residency. Dedicated can be provisioned in region.
[05:24] Ben: ok show me the numbers — send the spreadsheet.
[05:27] Samir: will do. Laura, do you want to talk benchmark specifics now?
[05:30] Laura: brief — we'll run two passes: hosted run against your 50k masked set with production concurrency, and a dedicated run on reserved capacity sized to your baseline QPS. We'll capture token counts, per-token cost, P50/P95 latency, and ops overhead.
[05:45] Marcus: timeline again?
[05:47] Laura: send data by Monday, we'll schedule hosted pass mid-week, dedicated run next week — results within 7-10 days.
[05:56] Ben: procurement timeline — we can review commercial by 3/18.
[05:59] Samir: sounds good. recap of next steps: Samir will send pricing spreadsheet and pilot terms, Laura will send benchmark plan, Galileo will share masked dataset and budget constraints.
[06:12] Aisha: thanks, that's helpful. one more thing: can you summarize the biggest levers to lower cost?
[06:17] Laura: summary — batching (latency tolerance), prefix/KV caching, model quantization + routing, and reserved capacity (Dedicated). Also workload shaping and caching at app level.
[06:29] Marcus: thanks all, we'll follow up shortly.
[06:33] Samir: appreciate your time, we'll follow up with docs and spreadsheet. bye.
